source_ref: https://osf.io/xbrnm/ ('Pictorial Materialism Test_girls.pdf', 'Pictorial Materialism Test_boys.pdf', 'Pictorial Materialism Test_database_clean.sav'); Trzcinska, Kubicka & Podsiadlowski (2023), PLOS ONE 18(8):e0290512, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0290512
note: Polish wording transcribed verbatim from the two OSF questionnaire PDFs; sentences were extracted programmatically from pdftotext output and each clause re-checked against the picture its item code names (128/128). Deviations from a literal transcript, all deliberate: (a) item_text and option_text concatenate the girls' and boys' forms with editorial '[girls' form]' / '[boys' form]' markers, because the item code does not record which gender-matched form a child saw; (b) option_text reproduces the item sentence's own clause for that picture, and the second clause is capitalised because in the source it appears mid-sentence; (c) instructions holds the PRZYKLAD practice item printed at the head of both forms, which is read to every child and is not scored (it is absent from the data). The .sav carries NO variable or value labels at all, so the mapping does not rest on labels: it rests on the pair abbreviation embedded in each ONE* column name (ZAB=zabawki, PREZ=prezent, PIEN=pieniadze, UBR=ubrania, RYS=rysowanie, CZYT=czytanie/bajka, KOL=kolezanki/koledzy, PLAC=plac zabaw), matched sentence by sentence against the PDFs, hence mapping_basis=reconstructed rather than data_labels. The 32 TWO* codes are the test-retest re-administration of the same items (n=27) and carry no pair abbreviation; their pairing to ONE* rests on the shared numeric suffix, corroborated but not individually pinned - see verification row. English assembled by IRW from the paper's own English; disclosed as machine_translation.
public_note: The Polish item text ships both gender-matched forms of every item in one field, marked [girls' form] and [boys' form], because the item code does not record which form a child saw; the 32 TWO* item codes are the same 32 questions re-administered two weeks later to a 27-child retest subsample rather than new items; and the English in the _translated columns was assembled by IRW from the paper's own English wording of each picture and question, not printed as sentences by the study.

source_ref: Piterova I (2024) Science-related populism: Psychometric properties of the Slovak version of the SciPop Scale. Ceskoslovenska psychologie 68(2):156-173, doi:10.51561/cspsych.68.2.156 -- 'Wording of questions' in Supplementary materials.pdf, OSF osf.io/yfx6h (CC BY 4.0), file 658022b6513a741e1aaed239; response file 'datacleaned_2023 ANONYM.xlsx', file 65141a1f333aef0229d7065b. English for Distrust2/Distrust3 from the same author's companion supplement, OSF osf.io/5aes7 file 6569c7ba43d06704a8b19e0a. Companion deposit osf.io/3w98r file 6543abf68a28b11bf6ffca58 used only to name four otherwise-undocumented blocks.
note: mapping_basis=paper_explicit: the OSF supplement's 'Wording of questions' table prefixes every reproduced item with the exact code the live table uses ('Ppl1: ...', 'Anti1: ...', 'TrustSc3: ...'), and those codes are verbatim the column headers of the deposit's response file 'datacleaned_2023 ANONYM.xlsx' (osf.io/yfx6h, file 65141a1f333aef0229d7065b) -- a label match, not an order inference. The xlsx itself carries no variable or value labels (plain code headers only), so this is NOT data_labels. No IRW processing script for this table exists in data/, but the code derivation is settled empirically: all 96 live item names are xlsx column names, and live per-item n/resp_min/resp_max/n_resp_levels equal the xlsx column's own four numbers for 96 of 96 items (irw_table_sets, server-side; no export). text_source=study_materials: item_text is the administered Slovak, item_text_translated the author's own English, both transcribed from the supplement ('Supplementary materials.pdf', osf.io/yfx6h file 658022b6513a741e1aaed239). translation_source=mixed because Distrust2/Distrust3's English comes from the same author's companion supplement (osf.io/5aes7) rather than this paper -- the supplement prints those two in Slovak only -- and the option-anchor English comes from the paper's Measures prose. DEVIATIONS from literal transcription, all deliberate: PDF line-wrap hyphenation and column breaks rejoined; the trailing reverse-scoring registered-sign glyph stripped from Distrust3; the supplement's missing terminal full stop on Homo3's English ('...values and interests') and Control2's Slovak preserved as printed. 63 of 96 items ship blank item_text -- see the notes row. VERIFIED NUMERICALLY: 20 of 20 published statistics reproduce to 2 dp from the columns the supplement labels (per-item means/SDs for PercSc1-4, TrustSc1-3, PolOr1, PolOr2; subscale means for SciPop total and its four factors, political populism and its three subscales, distrust of experts with Distrust3 reversed, relative deprivation), and Control2 -- whose own text instructs 'tick number two on the scale' -- takes the single value 2 for all 643 respondents.
public_note: Only 33 of this table's 96 items have published wording: the source deposit reproduces the items the SciPop validation paper reports, and the rest of the survey battery ships with item_text blank. The response anchors are not in the administered language either -- the Slovak labels are published nowhere, so option_text is blank and the author's English endpoint labels (e.g. 1 = fully disagree, 7 = fully agree) are recorded in option_text_translated instead. Homo2 is shared by two scales: it is also the SciPop scale's second 'ordinary people' item (Ppl2), administered once, so no separate Ppl2 item exists.

source_ref: poLCA 1.6.0 R package, data(election) + ?election Rd; ANES 2000 Time Series Pre-election Questionnaire w/ QxQ and Final Variable Nos., section K1z/K2/K3 (electionstudies.org/wp-content/uploads/2000/03/anes_timeseries_2000_qnaire_pre.pdf, retrieved via web.archive.org 2026-09-10)
note: Source is the `election` data frame shipped with CRAN package poLCA (2000 American National Election Study). data/polca.R melts election[,1:12] with item = names(x)[i], so the IRW item code IS the source column name (derivation pattern 1, no positional step), and sets resp <- as.numeric(substr(resp,1,1)) on the factor LABELS, whose own text is '1 Extremely well' .. '4 Not well at all' -- so both the resp integers and the option wording come straight from the data file's value labels. Column headers are trait+candidate mnemonics (MORAL/CARES/KNOW/LEAD/DISHON/INTEL x G=Gore, B=Bush); ?election lists the same six traits for the same two candidates. The item_text words are the ANES questionnaire's own trait list, K2a-K2f (Gore) and K3a-K3f (Bush), and the section_prompt/instructions are the K2/K3 stems and the K1z lead-in, transcribed verbatim. DEVIATIONS, all disclosed: (1) the questionnaire prints the trait list and the response options in ALL CAPS as interviewer-script formatting; case was normalised to sentence case, which is also how poLCA's own value labels render them ('Extremely well'), and no words were changed; (2) the questionnaire stem reads "the phrase 'he is K2'" where K2 is a fill token -- shipped as '<trait>' with the trait itself in item_text, per the piped-text rule; (3) the ANES battery has a 7th trait, 'OUT OF TOUCH WITH ORDINARY PEOPLE' (K2g/K3g), which poLCA does not include, so it is correctly absent. Step 3b: live item set is exactly the 12 Gore/Bush trait variables and resp is 1-4, matching this battery and no other instrument in the study. Rights: ANES is a publicly funded study that publishes its own questionnaires; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located on electionstudies.org, and no register row exists for ANES/NES.
